searchText: Bigger than this problem is that the number of miners would boat the beacon chain 6 fold what it is now. <vbuterin> Why? <@97774605351010304> posted in <#598292067260825641> that there were approximately 500K single miners now Accounted for issuing validators to miners will be hard to coordinate. Rewarding with Eth on Eth2 to pools who then could distribute would be much easier <@755590043632140352> also there are many 1-5 gpu miners who will not reach 32 eth fast enough around the time of the merge It could not be that hard if a miner would deposited validator and specify its index in block's extra data. It requires work on the beacon chain side mostly and indeed not that simple from technical point of view. don't 1-5 gpu miners join the mining pool? Does the validator have to be active? A miner could earn a 20 Ether deposit in to a validator, for example. They would need to top it up themselves, but that's better than just having a binary "32 or nothing" system. It doesn't have to be active, it might be a problem because exit hence withdrawal is possible from the active state only. But doesn't seem like a big deal. The problem of this solution is that taking in account all its complexity it doesn't give any guarantee on the result the blocks extra data is set by pools. they do join, there are quite a lot of them. You can pull the data from ethermine.org btw If we're talking about issuing extra rewards on the beacon chain accounted to each participant of mining pool then it's really complex and seems like hardly feasible thing. Pools may pay extra rewards out of their pocket to participants with some discount and own those validators completely. Alternatively, could the validators be created in an exited state (obviously this would require a HF), purely to enable transfer of the funds regardless of amount of Ether? And then anyone will be able to create such a validator, right? No, it would be irregular as per the HF requirement. You mean moving specific validators to exited status upon miners' request? i wouldn’t force miners (by rewarding them with validators) to actively stake because there are jurisdictions where staking is treated differently than mining. does it really require work on the beacon chain? could mining a block just call `deposit` on the deposit contract with minted ETH? That's a good point Meh, they can quit mining if they want. 🤷 Or they can change jurisdictions. 😬 A kind of in-protocol transaction that updates the state of deposit contract? Won't it pollute deposit contract state with a small deposits? (though, I am not a fan of this solution for other reasons, but I think "taxation issues" shouldn't be a reason to not choose a particular solution) A reward is not a reward if you cannot realize it. I guess, but I'm not sure if that's an issue I *doubt* we would see a significant decrease in hashpower solely by switching rewards from immediate to PoS deposits. I just don't see that as being a major factor in the majority of miner decision making processes. The idea is to issue _extra_ portion of rewards on the beacon chain and leave regular rewards on the PoW chain. But I agree with a fact that this complexity might not be worthwhile, because despite of being locked these funds can be sold anyway. Staked eth derivatives can be used for this purpose, can't they? are you referring to coins like rEth by rocketpool? yes, something like that and probably others. also, miner may specify the address of a 3rd party in withdrawal credentials in created validator, the other way of selling staked eth I don't understand what's the advantage of paying to a validator account instead of to an eth1 account through a contract after the merge. I think that we are overcomplicating things in order to make this trustless when we only need to have a few large miners to agree on a payment system, the others will be forced to accept There was an attempt to find a trustless solution from miners' and docking procedure standpoints. But apparently there is no one that satisfies this goal completely. There is no advantage in charging extra rewards to validator balance, especially taking in account the complexity of such a solution. I do like the idea of a fork on both eth1 and eth2 that includes a hash determined by ACDs to implement some minimal finality aspect on powchain before merge. We do of course introduce more risk at the social level to ensure all folks are upgraded in a narrow window. it also increases implementation complexity, not sure that this is worthwhile <vbuterin> Yeah the problem is that such a fork choice rule change would basically be about as complex as just doing the merge <@425572898787426305> Can you remind me, what is the shortest *reasonable* finality follow distance of PoW chain? Assuming we introduced PoS finality gadget on PoW chain. it doesn't have to be the shortest, it just has to be shorter than the time a long range attack will take - no attacker could get to the target block height weeks ahead, as they wouldn't have that long. It only needs to be checked in the first block of the merge - just as genesis has some unique checks The lowest reasonable follow distance for the PoW chain seems to be `16` blocks. Which results in about `~40` blocks to finality in the best case if `Eth1Data` voting algorithm is changed in a way that it can come to consensus on a new portion of data within one epoch What if we *don't* change the voting algorithm in that way? What would the follow distance be then? (so we come to consensus on Eth1Data in the *next* epoch) Not the next but within `64` epochs a per current spec. It would be `~2000` blocks 🤔 Even 2000 block finality *greatly* reduces the risks of deep reorg attacks. 40 blocks is certainly better, but if the engineering costs of PoS finality are sufficiently lower then even a 2000 block finality gives us some something very useful. Which is a specific number of blocks that are "in danger" as we approach The Merge, and gives us a concrete target for "how much do we need to pay for security at the end?". `Eth1Data` is currently not secured by the whole validator set, this is also should be considered under Vitalik's merge spec, does `eth1_data` become useless? if so, was this planned from the start? it would be entirely unmodified in that super minimal proposal so you would still process deposits with the voting mechanism and delay <vbuterin> Under my merge spec, the eth1data voting mechanism continues to exist but it's vestigial; a hard fork right after the merge would clean that up exist and function, right? <vbuterin> right <vbuterin> So technically I guess proposers could vote for a bad root that is the case today. does it change in this merge scenario? <vbuterin> it does not <vbuterin> Until the post-merge cleanup fork How fast can the post merge clean up fork be implemented? <vbuterin> theoretically we could start work on it in parallel, and have it out in 2-3 months? Presumably we would have the consensus clients refuse to vote on any eth1data that they don't believe is legitimate at least, right? So while PoS *could* come to consensus on an invalid block, it shouldn't be like right now where they very easily can, even without malice (IIUC)? I would not say that proposers can easily come to consensus on invalid eth1 block today, but after the merge proposers votes on these block become vestigial because the network has already voted on all of these blocks before, otherwise, they wouldn't be in the canonical chain “in 2-3 months” after the quick merge? Or from now? <vbuterin> after the quick merge after! 😊👍🏻 can they? the block has to be in the eth1 chain to be considered for voting per the spec <vbuterin> after the merge, the ethpow chain will continue to exist, it will just be embedded within the beacon chain (and without the pow) <vbuterin> So everything that involved talking to the ethpow chain will continue to work Most pools could offer "staked eth" as most plan to offer staking anyway. So miners could track their staking rewards through a similar page on their pool. This would also help pools to transition to staking and give them additional incentive to promote a smooth merge. This ETH could be credited/created post-merge so that it doesn't exist until after the merge.
